title: Independent Development Exception
where_to_look: The Confidential Information definition and its enumerated exceptions.
required: Require an independent-development exception limited to information developed by or for Receiving Party without use or reference to Disclosing Party's Confidential Information and supported by written records.
fallback: Accept the exception without the written-record requirement, but retain the express prohibition on use or reference to Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
escalate_if: Escalate if the exception permits independent development using or referencing Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
flag_if: The definition contains an independent-development exception.
The exception uses only a no-access or no-reliance standard.
The exception lacks an express prohibition on use or reference to Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
The exception lacks written-record support for an independent-development claim.
The exception applies to information developed by personnel who had access to Confidential Information.
preferred_language: Confidential Information does not include information independently developed by or for Receiving Party without use of or reference to Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, as demonstrated by contemporaneous written records.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 3 counterparties, consistent direction on prohibiting use or reference, with mixed support for written records.
matching_clause_names: Definition of Confidential InformationIndependent Development Exception

title: Trade Secret Inclusion in Confidential Information
where_to_look: Definition of Confidential Information and any provision addressing the duration or treatment of trade secrets.
required: Include trade secrets in Confidential Information only to the extent they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law.
fallback: Accept a general reference to trade secrets without the applicable-law qualifier if trade secrets remain expressly covered.
escalate_if: Escalate if the clause excludes trade secrets that qualify as such under applicable law.
flag_if: Trade secrets appear in the definition of Confidential Information.
Trade secrets are expressly limited to information qualifying under applicable law.
Trade secrets are covered without an applicable-law qualification.
Trade secrets are excluded unless marked or identified as confidential.
preferred_language: Confidential Information includes trade secrets that qualify as such under applicable law.
confidence_note: Based on 1 finding with a consistent direction, this position is provisional.
matching_clause_names: Definition of Confidential Information  Trade Secrets

title: Confidential Information Definition and Scope
where_to_look: Review the Confidential Information or Proprietary Information definition and its exclusions.
required: Require a definition limited to non-public information related to the Purpose, regardless of form or marking, including information learned by observation or inspection.
fallback: Accept a broader definition that remains tied to the Purpose and applies an objective reasonable-person standard to unmarked information with customary exclusions.
escalate_if: Escalate any definition that covers information unrelated to the Purpose or omits customary exclusions.
flag_if: The definition covers information without tying it to the Purpose or transaction.
The definition relies solely on confidentiality markings for protection.
The definition excludes information learned by observation or inspection.
The definition requires every oral disclosure to be confirmed in writing.
The definition lacks customary exclusions for public, prior-known, third-party, or independently developed information.
preferred_language: “Confidential Information” means non-public information related to the Purpose disclosed or made available by or on behalf of a Party in any form, whether written, oral, electronic, visual, or otherwise, including information learned through observation or inspection, and information not marked as confidential that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential based on its nature or the circumstances of disclosure.
confidence_note: Based on 49 findings, the issue is consistently negotiated, with recurring high-significance edits that both broaden and narrow scope.

title: General Confidentiality Exclusions and Carve-Outs
where_to_look: Confidential Information or Proprietary Information definitions and the exclusions or exceptions that follow them.
required: Require carve-outs for public information, prior non-confidential possession, lawful third-party receipt, and independent development by or for Recipient without use or reference to Confidential Information.
fallback: Accept the same carve-outs with reasonable-knowledge qualifiers for third-party rights and written-record support for prior possession or independent development.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting deletion of the exclusion framework or any carve-out that permits use of Confidential Information or excuses Recipient's wrongful disclosure.
flag_if: The definition treats all disclosed information as Confidential Information unless expressly excepted.
The exclusions omit information already possessed by Recipient on a non-confidential basis.
The third-party exclusion lacks a lawful-source or no-confidentiality condition.
The independent-development exclusion omits development by or for Recipient.
The public-domain exclusion does not address information that later becomes public through no act or omission of Recipient.
preferred_language: Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes generally available to the public other than through an act or omission of Recipient or its Representatives, was in Recipient’s possession on a non-confidential basis before disclosure, is lawfully received from a third party that has no obligation of confidentiality to Disclosing Party, or is independently developed by or for Recipient without use of or reference to Disclosing Party’s Confidential Information, in each case as demonstrated by written records.
confidence_note: Based on 49 findings across multiple counterparties, the direction is consistent on core carve-outs but mostly moderate in significance.
matching_clause_names: Confidential InformationDefinition, scope, and designation or marking requirements

title: Purpose Must Match the Contemplated Transaction
where_to_look: Preamble recitals and defined-term provisions describing the Purpose, Project, or business relationship.
required: Require a complete, transaction-specific Purpose tied to the contemplated products, services, project, or relationship, with use and disclosure limited to that Purpose.
fallback: Accept a broader business-relationship description only if it is complete, defined, and expressly limits use and disclosure to that relationship.
escalate_if: Escalate any Purpose that is blank, malformed, internally inconsistent, or permits unrelated future transactions.
flag_if: The Purpose contains a blank, placeholder, or incomplete phrase.
The Purpose refers only to a general business relationship without identifying the transaction subject.
The agreement permits use or disclosure beyond the defined Purpose.
The Purpose names a project, product, or service that does not match the transaction described elsewhere.
The agreement omits reciprocal disclosure where both parties are expected to exchange information.
preferred_language: “Purpose” means the parties’ evaluation, negotiation, and, if agreed, performance of [the specific transaction, products, services, project, or business relationship described here]. Each Party may use and disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information solely to accomplish the Purpose and may disclose it only to Representatives who need to know it for the Purpose.
confidence_note: Based on 19 findings across 19 counterparties, with a consistent direction toward a defined and tailored transaction scope.
matching_clause_names: Purpose Definition and Confidential Information Scope

title: Purpose-Limited Use and Need-to-Know Access
where_to_look: Look in the permitted-use, nonuse, nondisclosure, and copying provisions.
required: Require purpose-only use, need-to-know corporate access, and protection for all authorized copies.
fallback: Accept use for the defined Relationship and necessary internal access, provided every recipient is bound by confidentiality duties.
escalate_if: Escalate any unrestricted use right or disclosure right lacking a defined Purpose or confidentiality restriction.
flag_if: The recipient may use Confidential Information for any purpose other than the defined Purpose.
The recipient may use Confidential Information for its own unrelated benefit.
Disclosure to Representatives is allowed without a need-to-know restriction.
Corporate recipients are not required to protect Confidential Information under written confidentiality duties.
Copies or transcriptions are not treated as Confidential Information.
preferred_language: The Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose, shall not use it for any unrelated purpose or for the benefit of a third party, and shall disclose it only to its Representatives with a need to know for the Purpose who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Agreement; all copies and transcriptions made for the Purpose shall remain Confidential Information subject to this Agreement.
confidence_note: Based on 18 findings across 7 clause-name variants, with a consistent direction toward purpose-limited use, need-to-know access, and protected copies.
matching_clause_names: Permitted Use and Confidential Information Scope
Purpose and Use of Confidential Information
Treatment of Confidential InformationPermitted Disclosure and Use

title: Affiliate Scope, Status and Obligations
where_to_look: Affiliate definitions, Representative provisions, and permitted-disclosure sections.
required: Require that no Affiliate is deemed a Representative or has obligations unless it receives Confidential Information from or at a Party’s direction.
fallback: Accept covered Affiliate sharing only with need-to-know access, equivalent confidentiality duties, and contracting-party responsibility for compliance.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that automatically binds all Affiliates, imposes liability on non-recipient Affiliates, or permits unrestricted affiliate sharing.
flag_if: “Affiliate” is defined by ownership or control.
Affiliates are included within “Representatives,” “Discloser,” or “Recipient.”
The clause imposes obligations on Affiliates without requiring receipt of Confidential Information.
The clause permits disclosure to Affiliates without equivalent confidentiality obligations.
Board or personnel overlap is treated as receipt or disclosure by an Affiliate.
preferred_language: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no Affiliate of a Party shall be deemed that Party’s Representative or have any obligation under this Agreement unless such Affiliate receives Confidential Information from or at the direction of a Party; the Party making or directing the disclosure shall remain responsible for the Affiliate’s compliance.
confidence_note: Based on 33 findings across multiple counterparties, consistent high-significance direction toward a receipt-based Affiliate carve-out, with limited sharing and enforcement exceptions.
matching_clause_names: Affiliate Definition and Treatment of Affiliates

title: Confidentiality Marking and Designation Procedures
where_to_look: Confidential Information definitions and provisions governing marking and oral or visual disclosures.
required: Require reasonable efforts to mark tangible information and identify oral or visual disclosures, with written confirmation within 30 days.
fallback: Accept a reasonable-efforts procedure using similar designations, provided omitted marking or confirmation does not automatically eliminate confidentiality.
escalate_if: Escalate if the clause makes confidentiality depend solely on a mark or a 30-day written confirmation.
flag_if: The clause requires written materials to bear a Confidential legend.
The clause requires oral, visual, projected, or demonstrated information to be identified as confidential at disclosure.
The clause requires written confirmation of oral or visual confidentiality within 30 days.
The clause states that missing a mark or confirmation automatically defeats confidentiality.
preferred_language: The Disclosing Party shall use reasonable efforts to mark tangible Confidential Information as “Confidential” or with a similar designation, shall identify Confidential Information disclosed orally, visually, by demonstration, or through other media as confidential at the time of disclosure, and shall confirm that designation in writing delivered to the Receiving Party within thirty (30) days after disclosure; failure to mark or confirm does not remove confidential status when the nature or circumstances of disclosure reasonably indicate that the information is confidential.
confidence_note: Based on 4 findings across 4 counterparties, consistent direction with moderate procedural flexibility.
matching_clause_names: Confidentiality Designation and Oral Disclosure Procedure

title: Purpose-Limited Operational Copies
where_to_look: Look in no-copying, copying rights, reproduction, and use-of-confidential-information provisions.
required: Permit copying, reproduction, and transcription only when strictly necessary for the Purpose, with all permitted copies protected as Confidential Information.
fallback: Allow copies reasonably necessary for the Purpose, provided each copy remains subject to the NDA's confidentiality restrictions.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that permits copying outside the Purpose or fails to protect authorized copies and transcriptions as Confidential Information.
flag_if: The clause prohibits all copying or transcription without a Purpose-based exception.
The clause permits copying without limiting it to the Purpose.
The clause permits copies to be shared outside authorized recipients.
The clause fails to treat authorized copies and transcriptions as Confidential Information.
The clause omits prototypes, software, or other physical objects embodying Confidential Information from reproduction restrictions.
preferred_language: The Receiving Party shall not copy, reproduce, or transcribe Confidential Information, including any prototype, software, or other physical object embodying Confidential Information, except to the extent strictly necessary for the Purpose; all permitted copies, reproductions, and transcriptions shall be deemed Confidential Information and remain subject to the restrictions of this Agreement.
confidence_note: Based on 5 findings across 4 counterparties, including one duplicate record, the direction is consistent toward Purpose-limited operational copying with continued protection for copies.
matching_clause_names: Copying and Use of Confidential Information
Nondisclosure and Nonuse  Permitted Copies and Uses

title: Need-to-Know Representative Disclosures
where_to_look: Permitted disclosure, Representatives, affiliates, and need-to-know provisions.
required: Limit access to Representatives with a need to know for the Purpose, require equivalent written confidentiality duties, and retain responsibility for their breaches.
fallback: Permit customary employees and Representatives to rely on existing written confidentiality duties without requiring a separate acknowledgment, while retaining responsibility for their breaches.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision allowing affiliate or Representative access without a need-to-know limit and comparable confidentiality obligations.
flag_if: The clause permits disclosure to affiliates without a need-to-know limit.
The clause permits disclosure to Representatives without a need-to-know limit.
Representatives are not bound by this NDA or equivalent no-less-restrictive confidentiality duties.
The Receiving Party disclaims responsibility for Representative breaches.
Third-party disclosure is permitted without a confidentiality undertaking.
preferred_language: Receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information solely to its Affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees, consultants, agents, representatives, and professional advisers who have a bona fide need to know the Confidential Information for the Purpose, provided that each such person is informed of its confidential nature and is bound by this Agreement or written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth herein. Receiving Party remains responsible for any breach of this Agreement by each such person.
confidence_note: Based on 30 findings across 23 counterparties, consistent direction toward controlled need-to-know access and equivalent confidentiality obligations, with mixed treatment of affiliate scope and consent.

title: Transaction-Specific Non-Solicitation Limits
where_to_look: Review non-solicitation, non-interference, customer relationship, and return-or-destruction provisions.
required: Reject blanket restrictions and limit any retained restriction to knowing misuse of Confidential Information to solicit transaction-identified employees or customers.
fallback: Accept a 12-month restriction limited to knowingly soliciting employees or customers first identified through the transaction, with no ban on competition or ordinary business contact.
escalate_if: Escalate any restriction that reaches persons or relationships not learned through the transaction, restricts ordinary competition, or lacks a defined term.
flag_if: The clause bars soliciting or hiring any employee of the counterparty.
The clause restricts soliciting or diverting the counterparty’s customers.
The clause prohibits interference with the counterparty’s business relationships.
The clause applies without requiring use of Confidential Information.
The clause lacks a defined duration or transaction-based scope.
preferred_language: Neither Party shall be restricted from hiring, soliciting, competing with, or doing business with any person solely because of this Agreement; provided that, during the evaluation of the Potential Transaction and for 12 months thereafter, neither Party shall knowingly use the other Party’s Confidential Information to solicit for employment any employee or to solicit any customer of the other Party first identified through the evaluation.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 3 counterparties, the direction is mixed, with one narrowing, one broadening, and one deletion of restrictions.
matching_clause_names: Return or Destruction of Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation

title: Compelled Disclosure Notice and Legal-Permissibility Limits
where_to_look: Required-disclosure, subpoena, legal-process, and compelled-disclosure exceptions.
required: Require notice before disclosure to the extent legally permissible, Discloser-funded protective relief, counsel-limited production, and confidential-treatment assurances.
fallback: Accept legally permissible notice, counsel-limited disclosure, and reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment without an express cost allocation.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that eliminates legally permissible notice or permits disclosure beyond counsel’s required scope.
flag_if: The clause requires advance notice of compelled disclosure without a legal-permissibility qualifier.
The clause omits the Discloser’s opportunity to seek protective relief or waive compliance.
The clause permits disclosure of more information than counsel advises is required.
The clause omits efforts to obtain reliable confidential-treatment assurances.
The clause makes the Recipient bear protective-order or other protective-relief costs.
preferred_language: If Receiving Party is required by law, regulation, subpoena, court order, or other legal process to disclose Confidential Information, Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, promptly notify Disclosing Party before disclosure so that Disclosing Party may, at its sole expense, seek a protective order or other remedy or waive compliance with this Agreement. If no remedy limits disclosure, Receiving Party shall disclose only the portion counsel advises it must provide and shall seek reliable assurances of confidential treatment.
confidence_note: Based on 49 findings across multiple counterparties, the direction is consistent and predominantly high significance.
matching_clause_names: Required Disclosure  Scope and Confidential Treatment
Disclosure Required by Law  Notice and Expenses
Disclosure Required by Law  Confidential Treatment Assurances

title: Agreement Term, Expiration and Early Termination
where_to_look: Term, Termination, Expiration, and Survival provisions.
required: Require a one-year term with automatic expiration, mutual no-cause termination on 30 days’ written notice, and survival.
fallback: Accept a fixed term of up to three years, mutual 30-day termination, and express survival for confidentiality and trade secrets.
escalate_if: Escalate any indefinite term, one-sided or immediate termination right, or failure to preserve confidentiality and trade-secret obligations.
flag_if: The agreement has no stated expiration date.
The term continues until mutual written termination.
Only one party may terminate.
Termination is effective immediately upon notice.
Confidentiality obligations do not survive expiration or termination.
preferred_language: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall expire one (1) year thereafter, unless terminated earlier by either Party for any reason upon thirty (30) days’ written notice to the other Party; provided that the confidentiality obligations shall survive termination or expiration for three (3) years, and obligations concerning trade secrets shall continue for so long as the information remains a trade secret.
confidence_note: Based on 35 findings across 31 requests, the direction toward defined terms, mutual 30-day termination, and express survival is consistent, with variation in agreed term and survival length.

title: Trade Secret Survival Duration
where_to_look: Confidentiality survival, term and termination, or post-expiration obligations clause.
required: Require trade-secret confidentiality to continue for as long as the information qualifies under applicable law.
fallback: Accept a fixed five-year confidentiality period after termination or expiration for all Confidential Information.
escalate_if: Escalate if the agreement limits trade-secret protection to a fixed period shorter than five years.
flag_if: The survival clause sets one fixed duration for all Confidential Information.
The survival clause contains no trade-secret carve-out.
Trade-secret confidentiality ends on expiration or termination.
Trade-secret survival is perpetual without reference to applicable law.
The agreement provides less than five years of post-termination confidentiality.
preferred_language: Notwithstanding the expiration or termination of this Agreement, Recipient’s obligations with respect to Confidential Information shall continue for five (5) years after expiration or termination of this Agreement; provided, however, that Confidential Information that qualifies as a trade secret under applicable law shall remain confidential for so long as it qualifies as a trade secret.
confidence_note: Based on 11 findings across 10 counterparties, consistent direction toward protection for as long as information qualifies as a trade secret.
matching_clause_names: Confidentiality Duration and Trade Secret Survival

title: Return, Destruction and Retention Exceptions
where_to_look: Review the return, destruction, retention, archival-copy, and backup-media provisions.
required: Require prompt return or destruction, allowing only one archival copy for legal or compliance needs and non-segregable routine backups subject to confidentiality and ordinary-course deletion.
fallback: Accept a standard one-copy and backup exception for documented legal or compliance needs if all retained material remains confidential.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting unrestricted retention, business use, general employee access, indefinite retention, or unclear destruction obligations.
flag_if: The clause requires return or destruction of all copies without a retention exception.
The clause permits retention for legal, regulatory, compliance, audit, evidentiary, or document-retention purposes.
The clause permits retention of routine backups or information that cannot be readily located or segregated.
The clause fails to require retained information to remain confidential throughout retention.
The clause lacks an ordinary-course deletion rule for retained backup data.
preferred_language: Upon written request or termination, the Receiving Party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information and materials derived from it. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Receiving Party may retain one archival copy solely to satisfy legal, regulatory, compliance, audit, evidentiary, or document-retention requirements. The Receiving Party may also retain Confidential Information embedded in routine disaster-recovery or other backup media that is not reasonably capable of being readily located or segregated, which shall be deleted in the ordinary course of business. Access to retained Confidential Information shall be limited to personnel and advisers with a need to know for those purposes, no other use or disclosure shall be permitted, and all retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to this Agreement throughout the period of retention.
confidence_note: Based on 59 findings across numerous counterparties, the direction toward narrow retention and backup exceptions is consistent, with significance more often medium than high.
matching_clause_names: Return or Destruction of Confidential Information

title: Ordinary Confidentiality Survival Period
where_to_look: Review the Term, Termination, Survival, and post-termination confidentiality provisions.
required: Require confidentiality and non-use obligations to survive termination or expiration for five years, with trade-secret protection lasting while the information remains a trade secret.
fallback: Accept a three-year survival period from termination or expiration, with trade-secret protection lasting while the information remains a trade secret.
escalate_if: Escalate any indefinite, absent, conflicting, or unintelligible ordinary confidentiality survival period before acceptance.
flag_if: The clause states that ordinary confidentiality obligations continue indefinitely.
The clause omits an express survival period after termination or expiration.
The clause sets ordinary confidentiality survival shorter than three years.
The clause lacks protection for trade secrets while they qualify as trade secrets.
The clause contains conflicting or malformed duration language.
preferred_language: Notwithstanding termination or expiration of this Agreement, Receiving Party’s confidentiality and non-use obligations shall survive for five years from the date of termination or expiration; provided that Confidential Information qualifying as a trade secret under applicable law shall remain confidential for so long as it qualifies as a trade secret.
confidence_note: Based on 31 supplied findings across 26 counterparties, the direction is consistent toward finite three- or five-year ordinary survival with a trade-secret carve-out.
matching_clause_names: Term and Survival of Confidentiality Obligations

title: Security Incident Notification, Containment and Remediation
where_to_look: Look in notice, confidentiality remedies, security incident response, and data protection provisions.
required: Require immediate notice of any potential or actual Security Incident, prompt containment, and remedial action.
fallback: Accept notice as soon as reasonably practicable with reasonable containment and remediation duties.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that omits notice for potential incidents or permits delayed notice, containment, or remediation.
flag_if: The incident definition is limited to confirmed breaches.
The notice deadline exceeds 24 hours after discovery.
The clause omits containment duties.
The clause omits remediation duties.
Notice may be delayed until the investigation is complete.
preferred_language: Upon discovery of any potential or actual Security Incident, Recipient shall immediately notify Discloser and take all reasonably necessary steps to eliminate or contain the exposures that led to the Security Incident and take remedial action in accordance with Recipient’s security incident management policies and procedures and applicable Data Protection Laws and Regulations.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings across 4 counterparties, with consistent high-significance additions requiring immediate notice, containment, and remediation.
matching_clause_names: Notice of Security Incident and Remediation
Definitions (Data Protection Laws and Security Incident)

title: Confidentiality Safeguards and Standard of Care
where_to_look: Confidentiality, information-security, and recipient safeguarding provisions.
required: Require protection using the same care applied to the recipient’s comparable confidential information, with reasonable care as the floor.
fallback: Accept commercially reasonable efforts only if the clause retains an express reasonable-care floor and equivalent duties for authorized personnel.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that permits protection below reasonable care or access by persons without binding confidentiality obligations.
flag_if: The clause uses only a reasonable-efforts standard without a reasonable-care floor.
The clause lacks a same-care-as-own-information standard.
The clause disclaims responsibility for unauthorized access or disclosure.
The clause allows personnel or service providers to access information without equivalent confidentiality duties.
preferred_language: Recipient shall protect Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of like importance, and in no event less than reasonable care, to prevent loss, theft, unauthorized access, unauthorized use, dissemination, publication, or other disclosure.
confidence_note: Based on 20 listed findings across 11 counterparties, the direction is consistent toward a same-care standard with a reasonable-care floor, while significance is mostly medium.
matching_clause_names: Data Privacy and Information Security Safeguards

title: Protective Orders, Cooperation Costs and Disclosure Minimization
where_to_look: Look in compelled-disclosure, required-disclosure, legal-process, and protective-order provisions.
required: Require prompt notice to the extent legally permissible, Discloser-paid protective efforts, confidential treatment, and disclosure limited to the legal minimum.
fallback: Accept each party bearing its own costs while retaining lawful prompt notice, reasonable cooperation, confidential-treatment efforts, and disclosure limited to the legal minimum.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause imposing liability for a legally compelled disclosure or requiring disclosure beyond counsel-advised minimum.
flag_if: The notice duty lacks a legally permissible qualifier.
The clause requires the recipient to fund protective-order efforts.
The clause omits a duty to seek confidential treatment.
The recipient may disclose more than counsel advises is legally required.
The clause imposes contractual liability for a legally compelled disclosure.
preferred_language: If Receiving Party is legally required to disclose Confidential Information, it shall, to the extent legally permissible, promptly notify Disclosing Party and reasonably cooperate, at Disclosing Party’s sole expense, with Disclosing Party’s efforts to obtain a protective order or confidential treatment, disclose only the portion its counsel advises it is legally required to disclose, and have no liability under this Agreement for that limited disclosure if protection is unavailable.
confidence_note: Based on 12 findings across 5 counterparties, the direction is consistent but the findings are predominantly medium significance.
matching_clause_names: Required Disclosure  Scope and Confidential Treatment
Required Disclosure  Scope and Confidential Treatment

title: Reverse Engineering and Technical Exploitation Restrictions
where_to_look: Use restrictions and confidentiality provisions covering technical materials, prototypes, software, and IP filings.
required: Require Purpose-only use and prohibit reverse engineering, copying technical embodiments, and IP filings based on Confidential Information.
fallback: Accept Purpose-limited use with no reverse engineering or IP filing, allowing copies solely as necessary to perform the Purpose.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that permits reverse engineering or permits Confidential Information to be used in an intellectual-property filing.
flag_if: The clause permits reverse engineering.
The clause permits reverse compilation, decompilation, or disassembly.
The clause permits copying or reproducing technical embodiments of Confidential Information.
The clause permits use of Confidential Information in an intellectual-property application.
The use restriction does not limit Confidential Information to the Purpose.
preferred_language: The Receiving Party shall use Confidential Information solely for the Purpose and shall not reverse engineer, reverse compile, decompile, disassemble, or otherwise seek to derive proprietary information from any product, prototype, software, sample, or other object embodying Confidential Information, copy or reproduce such materials except as strictly necessary for the Purpose, or include Confidential Information in any patent, utility model, design, or other intellectual property application filed by or for the Receiving Party.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 2 counterparties, the direction is consistent, with two high-significance changes and one moderate change.
matching_clause_names: Obligation to Protect Confidential Information  Reverse Engineering
Obligation to Protect Confidential Information  Reverse Engineering

title: Indemnification and Defense Obligations
where_to_look: Indemnification, defense, security-breach, and remedies provisions.
required: Require reciprocal third-party indemnity and defense for losses caused by breach or culpable conduct, with defense control and settlement consent.
fallback: Accept third-party indemnity tied to breach or fault, with reasonable losses, prompt notice, defense control, and consent to adverse settlements.
escalate_if: Escalate first-party indemnity, uncapped indemnity exposure, or any right to settle without the indemnitee’s written consent.
flag_if: The indemnity covers claims other than third-party claims.
The trigger is not tied to the indemnifying party’s breach or culpable conduct.
The indemnifying party lacks control of the defense.
A settlement can bind the indemnified party without written consent.
The indemnity excludes reasonable defense costs or attorneys’ fees.
preferred_language: Each party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its affiliates and representatives from third-party claims and resulting reasonable losses, liabilities, defense costs, and attorneys’ fees to the extent caused by the indemnifying party’s breach, negligence, gross negligence, or willful misconduct; the indemnified party shall provide prompt notice and reasonable cooperation, the indemnifying party shall control the defense, and no settlement imposing liability or obligations on, or failing to fully release, the indemnified party may be made without its prior written consent.
confidence_note: Based on 17 reported findings across 4 counterparties, consistent high-stakes direction toward breach- or fault-based third-party indemnity and controlled defense.

title: Ownership, No License and Intellectual Property Reservation
where_to_look: Confidentiality, ownership, no-license, intellectual-property, and work-product provisions.
required: Require the Discloser to retain all right, title, and interest in Confidential Information and related IP, with no implied license.
fallback: Accept ownership language plus a license limited to the stated Purpose, with no transfer of ownership or broader implied rights.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that transfers ownership or grants a license in Marmon information or IP beyond the stated Purpose.
flag_if: The draft does not state that the Discloser retains ownership of Confidential Information.
The draft does not state that intellectual property in or reflected by Confidential Information remains reserved.
The draft grants Recipient an express or implied license beyond the stated Purpose.
The draft assigns or grants rights in work product, technology, inventions, or other intellectual property.
preferred_language: Discloser retains all right, title and interest in and to all Confidential Information disclosed, including any intellectual property contained or reflected therein or practiced thereby, and Recipient may use such Confidential Information solely for the Purpose; neither this Agreement nor any disclosure grants Recipient any other right or license, express or implied, in Discloser’s Confidential Information or related intellectual property.
confidence_note: Based on 13 findings across 9 counterparties, the negotiated direction consistently strengthens express ownership and no-license language, with some adjacent and ambiguous edits.

title: Independent Development and Similar-Product Safe Harbor
where_to_look: Look in NDA exceptions, independent development, residuals, and other developments provisions.
required: Require an express safe harbor for independently developed similar or competing products without use of Confidential Information.
fallback: Accept a safe harbor limited to independent development of similar or competing products, conditioned on full NDA compliance.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that authorizes use or disclosure of Confidential Information in developing or commercializing competing products.
flag_if: The NDA contains no express independent-development safe harbor.
The NDA prohibits products or services that compete with products described in the Confidential Information.
The NDA permits use or exploitation of information merely because it is similar to Confidential Information.
The NDA includes a residuals right to use remembered Confidential Information.
preferred_language: Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict Recipient from using information independently possessed or developed by Recipient, or from independently developing products or services that are similar to or compete with those contemplated by the Confidential Information, provided that Recipient does not use or disclose Discloser’s Confidential Information and continues to comply with this Agreement.
confidence_note: Based on 6 findings across 3 counterparties, all high significance and materially contested, with mixed final language.

title: Data Protection Laws and Personal Information
where_to_look: Review definitions, data-processing, security-incident notice, data-subject request, and transfer-remedy provisions.
required: Require instruction-bound processing, applicable-law compliance, security safeguards, prompt notices, segregation, and transfer remedies.
fallback: Accept applicable-law compliance, reasonable safeguards, prompt incident notice, and purpose-limited use without immediate termination rights.
escalate_if: Escalate if the counterparty rejects all limits on the use or disclosure of Personal Information.
flag_if: The draft lacks a defined term for Personal Information or Data Protection Laws.
The draft permits processing beyond the discloser's documented instructions.
The draft omits prompt notice of a Security Incident or individual request.
The draft lacks controls preventing access by unauthorized affiliates or representatives.
The draft omits suspension or termination rights for a material data-protection breach.
preferred_language: Recipient shall process Personal Information only on Discloser’s documented instructions and in compliance with all applicable privacy and data-security laws, maintain appropriate technical and organizational safeguards and prevent access by unauthorized affiliates and their representatives, promptly notify Discloser of any Security Incident, legally binding disclosure demand, or individual request concerning the Personal Information, and permit Discloser to suspend transfers or terminate this Agreement for a material breach of these obligations.
confidence_note: Based on 9 findings across 5 counterparties, this is a high-stakes and actively negotiated issue with a materially protective but mixed landing position.

title: Preserve Broad Equitable and Injunctive Relief
where_to_look: Remedies, enforcement, confidentiality breach, and irreparable-harm provisions.
required: Require express injunctive relief and specific performance for actual or threatened breaches without proving damages or posting bond.
fallback: Accept express injunctive and specific-performance rights for actual or threatened breaches without insisting on a bond waiver.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause that limits equitable relief to actual breaches or removes express injunctive relief entirely.
flag_if: The clause limits relief to actual breaches.
The clause omits threatened breaches.
The clause requires proof of actual damages before equitable relief.
The clause requires a bond or other security.
The clause deletes specific performance or other equitable relief.
preferred_language: Because a breach or threatened breach of this Agreement may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are inadequate, the non-breaching Party is entitled to seek injunctive relief and specific performance, without proving actual damages or posting bond or other security, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity.
confidence_note: Based on 17 listed findings representing 11 unique negotiations across 11 counterparties, the direction is moderately consistent: broad relief and bond waivers are often added, but one deletion and one softening show meaningful variation.

title: Confidential Information Accuracy and Warranty Disclaimer
where_to_look: Representations and warranties provisions and disclaimers following disclosure or return of Confidential Information.
required: Require the disclosing party to represent only its right to disclose and disclaim all other warranties, including accuracy and completeness, on an as-is basis, subject to express terms in a definitive agreement.
fallback: Accept a disclaimer limited to no representation or warranty regarding accuracy or completeness, while preserving express terms in a definitive agreement.
escalate_if: Escalate if the counterparty requires any warranty or affirmative representation regarding the Confidential Information’s accuracy, completeness, suitability, or use.
flag_if: The clause affirmatively represents that Confidential Information is accurate or complete.
The clause grants an accuracy or completeness warranty.
The clause lacks an as-is or no-warranty disclaimer.
The clause represents that disclosure will not conflict with future obligations.
preferred_language: Except for express representations and warranties set forth in a definitive written agreement executed by the parties, the Disclosing Party represents only that it has the right to disclose the Confidential Information; the Confidential Information is provided “AS IS,” and the Disclosing Party makes no other representation or warranty, express or implied, regarding its accuracy, completeness, suitability, or use, and disclaims all other warranties and guarantees of any kind.
confidence_note: Based on 7 findings, including two duplicated entries, the direction is consistent toward broad accuracy and warranty disclaimers, while one finding narrows future-obligation language.

title: Complete Legal Party Identity, Effective Date, and Execution
where_to_look: Review the preamble, party-identification and notice-address fields, Effective Date language, and signature blocks.
required: Require the exact legal name, entity type, formation jurisdiction, address, completed Effective Date, and matching authorized signature block for every party.
fallback: Accept a fixed completed Effective Date and omission of a business address only when every party’s legal identity and matching authorized signature details are complete.
escalate_if: Escalate if the final document has an entity-name mismatch, unclear party scope, an unsigned party, or an unresolvable Effective Date.
flag_if: Flag any blank or placeholder in a party’s legal name or address.
Flag any party description missing its entity type or jurisdiction of formation.
Flag any mismatch between a party name in the preamble and its signature block.
Flag any blank, undefined, or inconsistent Effective Date.
Flag any signature block missing the signer’s name, title, signature, or date.
preferred_language: This Agreement is entered into by and between the parties identified in the preamble by their full legal names, entity types, jurisdictions of formation, and business addresses, and is effective as of the date of the last signature below (the “Effective Date”); each party shall execute this Agreement through an authorized representative, and each signature block shall state the representative’s printed name, title, signature, and date.
confidence_note: Based on 61 reported findings across numerous counterparties, the direction is highly consistent toward completed entity, date, and execution details.

title: Fault-Based Liability and Damages Exclusions
where_to_look: Review limitation-of-liability, indemnification, and security-breach liability provisions.
required: Require mutual fault-based exposure for direct damages, a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, and carveouts preserving liability for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
fallback: Accept a one-sided damages exclusion only if it covers indirect damages alone, preserves direct-loss liability for breach or negligence, and does not protect gross negligence or willful misconduct.
escalate_if: Escalate any provision that protects gross negligence or willful misconduct, shifts the counterparty’s fault to Marmon, or leaves ordinary-breach exposure uncapped.
flag_if: The agreement lacks a consequential-damages exclusion.
The damages exclusion benefits only one party.
The clause imposes liability for any breach without a fault or causation qualifier.
The limitation protects gross negligence or willful misconduct.
The indemnity covers losses caused by the indemnitee or its Representatives.
preferred_language: Except for liability arising from a party’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, each party shall be liable only for direct damages caused by its breach or negligence, and neither party shall be liable for consequential, indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, or punitive damages, including lost profits, revenue, business opportunity, goodwill, or business interruption. Neither party shall be liable, and neither party shall be required to indemnify the other, to the extent a loss is caused by the other party or its Representatives.
confidence_note: Based on 15 findings across 5 counterparties, all high significance and largely consistent, with one reciprocal breach-indemnity formulation broader than the fault-based pattern.

title: Pricing, Product Schedules and Commercial Terms
where_to_look: Review order forms, product schedules, and fees, taxes, payment, cancellation, and refund provisions.
required: Require signed Orders to state all fees, payable without deduction or setoff, with no cancellation or refund rights and Customer responsible for transaction taxes.
fallback: Accept cancellation only for uncured Supplier breach and prorated refunds of prepaid unused fees, while preserving no-setoff and tax allocation.
escalate_if: Escalate any customer convenience termination, refund right unrelated to Supplier breach, or unilateral setoff right.
flag_if: Pricing is not stated in an Order or incorporated product schedule.
The customer may cancel an Order for convenience.
The customer may deduct or set off amounts against fees.
The agreement permits refunds of paid fees without Supplier breach.
The customer is not responsible for applicable transaction taxes.
preferred_language: Customer shall pay all fees set forth in each Order without deduction, setoff, or counterclaim. Once signed, each Order is non-cancelable, and all amounts paid are non-refundable, except as expressly stated in this Agreement. Customer shall pay all sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes arising from its purchases, excluding taxes based on Supplier’s net income.
confidence_note: Based on 1 finding with high significance, this position is provisional due to limited evidence.

title: Governing Law, Venue and Jurisdiction
where_to_look: Governing-law, jurisdiction, exclusive-venue, and dispute-resolution provisions.
required: Require a single Marmon-approved U.S. governing-law state, exclusive jurisdiction and venue in named state or federal courts, and a conflicts-of-law exclusion.
fallback: Accept a clearly identified U.S. governing law and exclusive named forum, even if the conflicts-law exclusion is omitted or the forum differs from the governing-law state.
escalate_if: Escalate any clause with conflicting jurisdiction names, an unspecified or non-exclusive forum, or malformed text obscuring the selected law or courts.
flag_if: The governing-law provision names more than one jurisdiction.
The clause permits venue in any court with personal jurisdiction over a party.
The clause does not state that venue or jurisdiction is exclusive.
The clause lacks an express conflicts-of-law exclusion.
Jurisdiction names are concatenated, incomplete, or grammatically malformed.
preferred_language: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the substantive laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in Delaware for any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement and waives any objection based on improper venue or inconvenient forum.
confidence_note: Based on 42 findings across 17 counterparties, the issue is consistently high-stakes and the need for a clear exclusive forum is consistent, but the selected jurisdictions are mixed.

title: Assignment and Transfer Consent Standards
where_to_look: Review the assignment, transfer, delegation, change-of-control, and successors-and-assigns provisions.
required: Require prior written consent for assignment, transfer, delegation, or change of control, with consent not unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and permit Affiliate and substantially-all-assets exceptions.
fallback: Accept prior written consent with consent not unreasonably withheld or delayed, while preserving defined Affiliate and substantially-all-assets exceptions.
escalate_if: Escalate if assignment or change of control is permitted without consent, or if consent is granted in the other Party’s sole discretion.
flag_if: The clause requires prior written consent for assignment or transfer.
The clause requires consent for delegation or change of control.
The consent standard bars unreasonable withholding or delay.
The clause permits assignment to an Affiliate or an acquirer of substantially all assets without consent.
The clause states that an unauthorized assignment is void.
preferred_language: Neither Party shall assign, transfer, delegate, or otherwise dispose of this Agreement or any rights or obligations under it, whether voluntarily, by operation of law, or through a change of control, without the other Party’s prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either Party may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, provided that the assignee assumes the assigning Party’s obligations under this Agreement.
confidence_note: Based on 52 findings, the direction is highly consistent toward retaining consent while prohibiting unreasonable withholding or delay, with limited support for Affiliate and asset-sale exceptions.

title: Jury Trial Waiver and Dispute Procedure Rights
where_to_look: Look in the governing-law, venue, dispute-resolution, jury-waiver, and prevailing-party-cost provisions.
required: Delete jury waivers and judge-only procedures, and reject automatic prevailing-party cost shifting.
fallback: Accept silence on jury trials and prevailing-party costs, but do not accept a judge-only requirement.
escalate_if: Escalate before accepting any express jury waiver, judge-only trial requirement, or automatic prevailing-party cost shifting.
flag_if: The dispute provision states that either party waives a right to trial by jury.
The dispute provision requires trial by a judge without a jury.
The jury waiver appears after an exclusive venue or governing-law provision.
The provision requires the losing party to reimburse the prevailing party's enforcement or litigation costs.
preferred_language: Each party retains its right to trial by jury in any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and no party waives that right; neither party shall recover attorneys' fees or other costs solely because it is the prevailing party.
confidence_note: Based on 3 findings across 2 counterparties, including one duplicate entry, the direction is consistent and high-significance.
